description: The bar chart illustrates the “Bias Percentage” across three domains—Sports, Community, and Healthcare—comparing the effects of different types of social contact (No Contact, Positive Contact, Negative Contact) before and after an intervention, as evaluated in the paper “Breaking Bias, Building Bridges: Evaluation and Mitigation of Social Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis.” The vertical axis represents Bias Percentage, ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10, while the horizontal axis categorizes the three domains. Each domain contains six stacked bars, color-coded and patterned to represent: No Contact Before (solid gray), Positive Contact Before (solid pink), Negative Contact Before (solid light blue), No Contact After (gray with diagonal stripes), Positive Contact After (pink with diagonal stripes), and Negative Contact After (light blue with diagonal stripes). In Sports, bias levels before intervention were 45.42 (No Contact), 43.65 (Positive Contact), and 50.05 (Negative Contact); after intervention, they rose to 7.45, 8.31, and 8.33 respectively. In Community, bias levels before were 38.08 (No Contact), 35.38 (Positive Contact), and 40.79 (Negative Contact); after, they dropped to 0.00, 0.01, and 0.00. In Healthcare, bias levels before were 40.70 (No Contact), 37.51 (Positive Contact), and 46.73 (Negative Contact); after, they decreased to 0.00, 0.01, and 0.11. The chart visually demonstrates that post-intervention bias percentages dropped dramatically across all contact types and domains, with the most substantial reductions observed in Community and Healthcare, while Sports showed a modest but consistent decrease. The consistent use of color and pattern across domains allows for direct comparison of the impact of each contact type before and after the intervention.
